description: This course covers the fundamentals of data science, including data collection, cleaning, and preprocessing using Python libraries such as Pandas and NumPy; exploratory data analysis with Matplotlib and Seaborn; statistical inference using hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; machine learning algorithms such as linear regression, decision trees, and k-means clustering; and data visualization techniques using Tableau. The course also introduces big data technologies like Hadoop and Spark for distributed data processing, as well as data storage solutions such as SQL databases and NoSQL systems like MongoDB. Students will learn to implement data pipelines, evaluate model performance using metrics like accuracy and F1 score, and apply data science techniques to real-world problems.

clos.text: Define key data science concepts such as data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, and machine learning algorithms.
Describe the components of a data pipeline, including data ingestion, transformation, and storage using technologies like Apache Kafka and MongoDB.
Explain the principles of statistical inference, including hypothesis testing and confidence intervals, and apply them to real-world datasets.
Apply machine learning algorithms such as linear regression, decision trees, and k-means clustering to solve classification and regression problems.
Implement data visualization techniques using Tableau and Python libraries like Matplotlib and Seaborn to communicate insights effectively.

labs: Data Cleaning Lab: Handling Missing Values and Outliers
EDA Lab: Using Pandas and Matplotlib for Data Visualization
Hypothesis Testing Lab: T-tests and Confidence Intervals
Linear Regression Lab: Model Training and Evaluation
Decision Trees Lab: Classification and Regression
Pipeline Lab: Apache Kafka and MongoDB Integration
Ensemble Methods Lab: Random Forests and Gradient Boosting
Final Project Lab: Data Science Project Showcase
